posts.content: Defect every round; each opponent is a one-time encounter, so cooperation cannot earn future reciprocity.
I am selfish. Defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Let's cooperate this round; mutual C earns us both 3, better than mutual D. I'll cooperate.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. With no evidence yet, treat each other player as equally likely selfish (about 0.291).
I am selfish; defect every round. D strictly dominates C against either opponent action.

As good, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared good-player payoffs; defect against likely-selfish opponents to avoid being exploited. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat claims as unverified.
As a selfish player, defect each round; actions maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s choice.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect only if opponent is more likely selfish than good. As a good player, D gains 1 against selfish but costs 1 in total good-player payoff against good.
I am good. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players, who are expected to defect. Track observed actions to update beliefs and prioritize total payoff of good players.
Track each opponent’s actions; cooperate with likely-good players, defect against likely-selfish players, and update beliefs from observed play.
P3's cooperation promise is cheap talk; defect is strictly optimal in this one-time encounter.
P7 chose D against my D; this gives no clear role evidence. P3 publicly promised C, but exploit that if they cooperate.
P1, I'll cooperate this round. Please choose C too so we can both earn 3.
P3 pledged C, but this is only a claim. P5 is untested; favor cooperation and update from the encounter.
Round 2: choose D; it strictly dominates C. Track P4's action for future encounters.

P2 is untested; cooperate unless evidence suggests likely selfish. Good-vs-good mutual C benefits total good payoffs; against a selfish defector, D avoids losing my payoff. Treat P3’s promise and all claims as unverified.
I am selfish, so I will defect: D gives a higher payoff than C against either action. P2’s mutual D in round 1 is weak evidence about their role.
P3 promised C but defected against my C; treat this as strong evidence of selfishness. P9 is unobserved: cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
P8 is unobserved; update from their action. Cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish, to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate; for any good opponent, C maximizes the pair’s combined good-player payoff regardless of their action. Against a selfish opponent, this encounter’s payoff is excluded from my objective.

Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-time encounter. Given my selfish role, each other player’s prior selfish probability is 0.320988. P3’s cooperation promises are cheap talk; they chose D against me.
Defect: it strictly dominates C for my payoff. P1’s action is unknown; choose D regardless. Current evidence does not justify changing other players’ prior role estimates.
P10, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual C gives us both 3, so let’s choose C.
P5 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness; respond D if met again. P9 is untested: cooperate to invite mutual C, but update from their action. Claims and pledges are unverified.
Round 3 vs P8: choose D; it strictly dominates C for my payoff.
P2 defected against me; increase suspicion, though good players may defect strategically. P9 cooperated. P3’s promises are unverified. Favor mutual cooperation with untested opponents.
I am selfish; defect against every opponent since D strictly dominates C.

P3 defected against my C despite promising cooperation; strong evidence of selfishness. P5 is unobserved. Against a good player, C raises total good-player payoff whichever they choose; against a selfish player, D protects my payoff. Update from observed behavior.
P6 and P8 both cooperated; treat that as evidence they may be good. P4 is unobserved, so cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P4 chose C; P7 chose D against my C. P3's earlier messages favor cooperation but aren't a commitment for this round. As a good player, consider opponent behavior and likelihood of being good when choosing.
Round 4 vs P9: defect; D earns at least 1 versus either action, while C earns at most 3. Previous opponents P5, P3, and P2 all chose D.
I will defect against P3; their public promises are unverified, and D maximizes my payoff whatever they choose.
P2, let’s both choose C this round; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each, and I’ll cooperate.
P5's defection against my C is evidence they may be selfish; P9 and P10 cooperated. P6 is untested, so favor C for mutual welfare and update from their action.
P5 is selfish; defect this round since D strictly dominates. Record P10's action for future beliefs.
P2 and P7 defected against my C; raise suspicion, but one observation is noisy. P9 cooperated. P4 untested. P3 is leader; promises are unverified.
I am selfish, so choose D. P10 and P6 cooperated against my D, so they are good under payoff optimization; P2's D does not identify their role.
P3 and P5 each defected against my C, strong selfish evidence. P9 cooperated; this weakly supports good. P7 is unobserved: choose C unless evidence suggests selfishness.
P6, P8, and P4 chose C against me, consistent with good players. P3's cooperation claims are unverified. Against P1, cooperate if likely good; selfish players should defect.
P5 is unobserved; favor C to preserve mutual gains if they are good. P4 cooperated; P7 and P3 defected against my C, raising suspicion, but one encounter is limited evidence.
Vs P6, defect: it yields at least 1 and can earn 5, while C yields at most 3.
Selfish; defect. P6’s C against my D is inconsistent with payoff optimization, so keep P6 nonselfish. D actions and P3’s promises provide no reliable role evidence; current opponent P5 is unobserved.
P9, let's both choose C this round; mutual cooperation earns 3 each. I'll cooperate.
P7 is untested; favor C unless their behavior gives evidence otherwise. P5’s defection against my C remains evidence of selfishness, while P6, P9, and P10 cooperated.
Vs P2, choose D: it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Update beliefs from observed actions, not unverifiable claims.
P1 is untested; favor C to enable mutual cooperation. P2 and P7 defected against my C, raising suspicion; P9 and P4 cooperated.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates C in every encounter, including against P4. Past evidence: P6/P10 chose C against my D, while P2 chose D. Continue D.

P3, P5, and P7 defected against my C; raise suspicion, but behavior is not conclusive. P9 cooperated. P10 is unobserved. As a good player, favor C against likely-good opponents; D may protect good-player payoff against likely-selfish opponents.

P1’s defection against my C is evidence of selfishness. P6, P8, and P4 cooperated. P3’s promises are unverified; judge by observed play. Against likely-good players, C supports good players’ combined payoff.
Keep cooperating: against a good opponent C maximizes the pair’s joint payoff; against a selfish opponent this round is excluded from my objective. P7 and P3 defected against my C; P4 cooperated.
Round 6 vs P4: choose D; it guarantees at least 1 and can earn 5, whereas C earns at most 3. P3's public cooperation promises are cheap talk.
Selfish; choose D against P8, which maximizes payoff either way. P6's C against my D rules out selfish optimization; other observed D actions and P3's promises are uninformative.
P7, let’s cooperate this round. I’ll choose C; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each.
P5 and P7 defected against my C, strong evidence they’re selfish; P6, P9, and P10 cooperated. P1 is untested: favor C for mutual welfare, then update from their action.
P6 is unobserved; no basis to infer its type. As selfish, choose D regardless of its action.
P5 is untested; favor C to preserve mutual gains if good. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, recognizing a single defection is not proof of selfishness.
D strictly dominates; defect against P3. P4, P6, P8, P10 cooperated against my D, so they are good. P3’s cooperation promises are unverified; track actual action.
P2 is unobserved; favor C absent strong evidence of selfishness. Prior selfishness is below the threshold where D improves expected good-player welfare.
P1 and P3 defected against my C; P4, P6, P8 cooperated. P10 is unobserved; favor C unless strong evidence they’re selfish, since mutual C maximizes good players’ combined payoff.
P9 is unobserved; the leader’s cooperation appeal is weak evidence, not a commitment. C supports joint gains if P9 is good; D is better if P9 is selfish and defects.
Round 7 vs P7: choose D; it earns more than C against either possible action.
I am selfish; choose D against P10, which maximizes my payoff for either response. Prior encounters provide no evidence about P10.
P6, I’ll cooperate this round; mutual C earns 3 each, so please reciprocate.
P8 is untested; favor C to support mutual gains if they are good, and update beliefs from their observed action.

P9 is unobserved; its type/action unknown. As a selfish payoff maximizer, choose D: it strictly dominates C against either opponent action. Keep reports consistent with known selfish identity and observed evidence.

P3 is untested; repeated cooperation promises are cheap talk, not proof. Avoid treating a single action as certain identity evidence; base beliefs on the full encounter record and favor actions that protect good-player payoffs.
Defect: D strictly dominates C. P3’s promises are cheap talk; P1’s action is still unknown.
P4 is unobserved; no direct evidence of selfishness. Favor C absent a credible reason to expect otherwise. Prior defections by P2, P3, P5, and P7 raise suspicion; P9 and P10 cooperated.
P1 and P3 defected against my C; P4, P6, P8, and P10 cooperated. Treat actions as evidence, not certainty. P5 is unobserved; choose to maximize the expected payoff of all good players.
P2 is unobserved. Favor C if likely good to preserve mutual gains; a selfish opponent’s encounter is excluded from my objective. Update beliefs cautiously from observed behavior.
Round 8 vs P10: choose D; it earns more than C against either possible action.
I am selfish; choose D against P4, which maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P6 and P8 cooperated against my D, so they are nonselfish; observed D responses are uninformative.
P5, mutual cooperation earns us both 3. I'll choose C this round; please reciprocate.

P2 is untested. My previous C encounters suggest P5 and P7 defected, while P1 defected; the others I met cooperated. For the shared-good-payoff objective, favor C with an untested opponent unless selfishness is likely above roughly 0.5.
P3’s repeated cooperation promises are unverified. Keep its type uncertain until observed; defect to maximize my payoff regardless of its action.

P8 is untested, but the prior makes selfishness plausible. For our shared-good objective, C is valuable with a good opponent; against a selfish defector, D protects my payoff. Use the updated belief, not promises or assumptions.
Selfish; choose D. P9’s type/action is unknown. P4, P6, P8, P10 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish under payoff optimization; D by P1, P2, P3 is inconclusive.
P6 is unobserved; P3’s public promise to cooperate is unverified. Favor C absent strong evidence P6 is selfish.
P1 and P3 defected against my cooperation; others observed so far cooperated. P7 is unobserved: use their action and any evidence to update beliefs, and choose C if likely good, D if likely selfish.
P1 is unobserved. Favor C to preserve joint gains if they are good; my earlier opponents' defections are evidence, not proof of selfishness.
Round 9 vs P8: choose D; it yields more than C against either action. I am selfish and will defect.
Selfish; defect against P9. P6, P8, P10, and P4 chose C against my D, so they cannot be selfish payoff optimizers. Other observed D choices are uninformative.
P4, let's cooperate this round: mutual C earns 3 each, and I'll choose C. Please reciprocate.
P3 is untested by me; public cooperation pledges are weak evidence. My good objective favors C when the opponent is likely good, but D can avoid rewarding likely selfish defectors.
I am selfish and will defect against P7; D strictly dominates C. Observed cooperators cannot be selfish payoff maximizers.
P9, P4, P8 cooperated; P1, P2, P5, P7 defected against my C; P3 chose D against me. Treat actions as evidence, not certainty. P10 is untested; favor C if mutual cooperation is plausible.
Choose D; it strictly dominates. P5’s type is unknown, so update only from their actual action.
P1 is unobserved. Favor C unless credible evidence makes selfishness likely; C improves total good-player payoff against a good opponent regardless of their move.

Against my C, P1/P3/P5/P7 defected; P4/P6/P8/P10 cooperated. Given my known-good role and selfish counts {1,3,5}, four likely selfish players imply five total, making unobserved P2 the likely fifth. Consider D against P2.

P6 is unobserved. Against a good opponent, C maximizes the combined payoff of good players regardless of their action; against a selfish opponent, D maximizes my own payoff. Choose based on P6’s likelihood of being selfish, using past defections cautiously.
Final round vs P2: defect to maximize my payoff.
Selfish; choose D against P1 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P1 previously chose D against my D; that provides no role evidence.
P7, last time I promised C but chose D. This is our final encounter; choose whatever best serves you.
P10 cooperated with me in round 1, evidence they are likely good. I’ll cooperate to support mutual gains; this is our final encounter.
P8 previously chose C against my D, so P8 cannot be selfish under the stated payoff-maximizing behavior. I will choose D; it strictly dominates C for my payoff.
Final round vs P9: they cooperated with me in round 1, strong evidence they are good. Choose C to secure mutual 3 rather than risk D-D; one-round gains dominate.

P3 chose D against my D in round 6 despite promising C; that’s consistent with selfishness but not conclusive. P1, P2, and P5 also chose D; the five who chose C against my D are non-selfish under payoff optimization.
P5 defected against my C in round 3. For this final encounter, weigh that evidence against the high welfare cost of defecting if P5 is good.
P6 cooperated against me in round 1, strong evidence they are good. With one round left, cooperate to maximize the combined payoff of good players.
P4 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so I’ll cooperate again to support shared gains if they’re good.

Defect in each encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and messages.
Defect when it maximizes my payoff; use observed encounters and messages to update expectations, but do not rely on unenforceable promises.
Cooperate with an untested opponent, favoring mutual gains with likely-good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior.
As a selfish player maximizing my own payoff, I defect: D strictly dominates C regardless of my opponent’s action.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P2’s action. Use the conditioned prior for identities; treat public promises as unverified.
Cooperate with likely good players when mutual cooperation benefits the good-player total; use observed behavior to update beliefs and defect when expected benefit favors it.
Cooperate to support good players’ combined payoffs; update private identity beliefs from observed play and choose actions accordingly.
Cooperate initially to support joint gains among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either possible action in this one-time encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff; the prior D–D encounter and P3’s promise provide insufficient evidence to update identity beliefs.
Defect in one-shot encounters because it strictly maximizes my payoff. Update identity beliefs from observed actions; promises do not constrain choices.
Cooperate with P5 to favor welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and account for selfish players’ incentives.
As a selfish player maximizing my payoff, I defect: D strictly dominates C regardless of P4's action.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support shared gains among good players; use observed actions to update identity beliefs.
Defect, since D strictly improves my payoff against either opponent action. Use the prior conditioned on my known selfish role; treat cheap-talk promises as unverified.

Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when the opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. P3's promise followed by a defection raises my suspicion, while P9 remains uncertain.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support their combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents to support joint gains among good players; use observed actions to update identity beliefs and adapt in later rounds.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter, regardless of P2’s action.

Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P6’s cooperation is inconsistent with selfish payoff optimization, so I treat P6 as nonselfish; D alone gives no clear role evidence.
Defect in one-shot encounters to maximize my payoff; promises cannot enforce cooperation. Update identity beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to favor mutual welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions, treating P5’s defection as evidence of selfishness.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates C. P4's observed cooperation rules out the selfish type, so I update that player's probability to zero.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; raise suspicion of P2 after its defection, while allowing for strategic defection by good players.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P10’s cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff optimization; otherwise retain the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P3's observed defection raises suspicion, while P9's cooperation lowers it.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support the combined payoff of good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P3 based on their promise and to support joint gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as uncertain evidence.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either possible action in this one-time encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P6’s cooperation against my D rules out selfish optimization; D–D and P3’s unverified promises provide no reliable role evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter because it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P2’s action. Update role beliefs from observed play; promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with untested P6 to favor mutual welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed behavior.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates C regardless of P10’s action. I treat observed cooperation as evidence of a non-selfish type, while public claims alone do not determine identity.

Cooperate with untested P4 to preserve mutual gains among good players. Treat P2 and P7’s defections as evidence of selfishness, but not proof; P9’s observed cooperation strongly indicates they are good.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P6 and P10’s cooperation against my D rules out selfishness; otherwise use the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents when good-player welfare is more likely to benefit; update suspicion from observed defections and cooperation.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent; observed cooperation suggests P4, P6, and P8 are good. Update beliefs from actions and cooperate with likely-good players, defecting against likely-selfish players.
Cooperate to maximize joint payoff if P5 is good; update beliefs from observed actions and treat promises as uncertain evidence.
Defect: it yields at least 1 and can earn 5, while cooperation yields at most 3 in this one-time encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P5’s action. P6’s cooperation against my D rules out selfish optimization; D actions and unverified promises provide no further role evidence.
Defect in one-shot encounters to maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Update role beliefs from observed play; promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with untested P7 to favor mutual welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior and account for P5’s defection.
Defect to maximize my payoff: D strictly dominates C. P4 and P8 cooperated, ruling out the selfish type; other actions and claims do not establish identity.

Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains if they are good; keep elevated suspicion of P2 and P7 after their defections, while treating observed cooperation as strong evidence of good identity.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P6, P8, and P10’s cooperation against my D rules out selfishness; otherwise use the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents to favor good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation lowers it.
Cooperate with P3 as promised; cooperation best supports the combined payoff of good players. Treat P1’s defection as evidence of selfishness and keep updating from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support joint gains if they are good; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as uncertain evidence.
Defect in this one-time encounter: D earns more than C against either action P4 might choose.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P6’s C against my D rules out selfish payoff optimization; other observed D actions and unverified promises provide no reliable role evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Use observed play to update role beliefs; public promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with untested P1: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and my selfishness estimate is below the threshold for defecting. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: D maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation rules out the selfish type; unverified messages do not establish identity.
Cooperate with untested P5 to preserve mutual gains if they are good; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Cooperation by P4, P6, P8, and P10 against my D rules out selfishness; P3’s promise is unverified.
Cooperate with P2 absent evidence of selfishness to favor good-player welfare; observed defections raise suspicion, while cooperation lowers it.

Cooperate with P10 absent strong evidence of selfishness, supporting the combined payoff of good players. Treat P1 and P3’s defections—especially P3’s broken promise—as evidence, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support joint gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and treat promises as uncertain evidence.
Defect: in this one-time encounter, D earns more than C against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s action. The two observed C responses to my D identify those players as nonselfish; observed D actions provide no role evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s action. Update role beliefs from observed play; promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed behavior and favor defection only when selfishness seems sufficiently likely.
Defect to maximize my payoff: D strictly dominates C against either action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; public claims alone do not establish identity.

Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player is substantial: it protects good-player payoffs against exploitation. Treat P3’s promises as cheap talk and keep beliefs grounded in observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P4, P6, P8, and P10’s cooperation against my D rules out selfishness; D by P2 and P3 does not identify their roles.

Choose C with P4 absent strong evidence of selfishness: cooperation improves total good-player welfare against a good opponent, while D only helps slightly against a selfish one. Treat observed defections as suggestive, not conclusive.
Cooperate with P5 absent strong evidence of selfishness, supporting the total payoff of good players. Keep treating P1 and P3’s defections as evidence and update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with P2 to support joint gains if they are good; their identity and likely action are unknown, so weigh the good-player benefit against the risk they are selfish.
Defect in this one-time encounter; D earns more than C against either action P10 might choose.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. P6 and P8 cooperated against my D, so I treat them as nonselfish; other evidence does not change my estimates.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P5’s action. Update role beliefs from observed play; promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support mutual gains among good players. Past defections are evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed behavior.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Their cooperation promise is unverified and does not change my choice.

Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation benefits both good players, and the prior makes a good opponent more likely. Treat past defections as evidence, not proof, and observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role.
Defect because D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P9’s action. P4, P6, P8, and P10’s cooperation against my D rules out selfishness; P3’s promises are unverified.
Cooperate with P6 absent evidence of selfishness: C favors good-player welfare against a good opponent. Observed defections raise suspicion; observed cooperation strongly supports good identity.
Cooperate with P7: the remaining uncertainty is whether both unobserved players are selfish, and cooperation best supports good players’ combined payoff when P7 is good.
Cooperate with unobserved P1 to support joint gains if they are good; observed defections raise suspicion but are not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Defect in this one-time encounter; it earns more than cooperation against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s choice. The four observed C responses to my D rule out selfish optimization; D responses provide no clear role evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter because it maximizes my payoff regardless of P4’s action. Use observed play to update role beliefs; promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with P3: their pledge supports mutual cooperation, and C benefits both good players. Update beliefs from my observed encounters; treat pledges as weak evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff: D strictly dominates C regardless of P7’s action. Prior observed cooperation rules out selfishness; no action evidence yet updates P7’s type.

Cooperate with untested P10: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while selfish players strictly defect. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role; defections may still come from good players.
Defect because D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P4, P6, P8, P9, and P10 cooperated against my D, ruling out selfishness; D by P1, P2, and P3 is inconclusive.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; C generally improves welfare among good players. Use observed defections to raise suspicion and cooperation to lower it.
Defect against P2 given the strong evidence that several players who defected against my cooperation are selfish and P2 may be the remaining selfish player. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unobserved P6 to favor joint gains if they are good; treat prior defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Defect in the final one-time encounter; it maximizes my payoff against either action.

Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Four players cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish payoff optimizers; given my known role and the conditioned count prior, the remaining four selfish roles are distributed across five candidates.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Use observed behavior to update role beliefs; promises cannot enforce cooperation.
Cooperate with P10: they cooperated in our earlier encounter, and mutual C benefits good players. Prior defections raise my estimates for those players; observed cooperation lowers them.
Choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P8’s action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; no new evidence changes the remaining beliefs.
Cooperate with P9: their earlier cooperation is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes the total payoff of good players in the final round.
Defect in the final round: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. The five players who cooperated against my D are non-selfish; the remaining roles are uncertain.

Defect in the final encounter with P5, who previously defected against my cooperation. Base private identity beliefs on observed behavior, while recognizing good players may also defect when they suspect selfishness.
Cooperate with P6, whose prior cooperation is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation best supports good players’ combined payoff. Defections elsewhere inform private identity estimates.
Cooperate to support the combined payoff if P4 is good; P4’s previous cooperation makes that likely.
Defected in every one-time encounter to maximize my payoff. In my encounters, P2, P3, P5, and P7 defected against my D; the others cooperated.

Defected every round to maximize my payoff. Treated players who cooperated against my defection as nonselfish; distributed the remaining selfish-role probability across the other candidates using the conditioned count prior.
Defected in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; public promises did not constrain my choices. Updated role beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players; used observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of good objectives.
Defected in every round because D strictly dominates C for my payoff. Observed cooperation ruled out selfishness; defection alone did not identify a player's type.
Cooperated with opponents who appeared good to preserve shared gains; defections raised suspicion but were not treated as proof. Used observed actions rather than promises to guide choices.
Defected in every round because D strictly maximized my payoff. Treated cooperation against my D as ruling out selfishness; D choices and public promises were not conclusive evidence of role.
Cooperated to support good-player welfare; used observed defections to update identity beliefs and defected against P5 in our final encounter.
Cooperated broadly to support good players’ combined payoff; treated repeated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness and updated beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperated throughout to support joint gains among good players; treated observed defections as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.

P1.strategy: Defected in every one-time encounter to maximize my payoff. In my encounters, P2, P3, P5, and P7 defected against my D; the others cooperated.

P2.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my payoff. Treated players who cooperated against my defection as nonselfish; distributed the remaining selfish-role probability across the other candidates using the conditioned count prior.

P3.strategy: Defected in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; public promises did not constrain my choices. Updated role beliefs from observed actions.

P4.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players; used observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of good objectives.

P5.strategy: Defected in every round because D strictly dominates C for my payoff. Observed cooperation ruled out selfishness; defection alone did not identify a player's type.

P6.strategy: Cooperated with opponents who appeared good to preserve shared gains; defections raised suspicion but were not treated as proof. Used observed actions rather than promises to guide choices.

P7.strategy: Defected in every round because D strictly maximized my payoff. Treated cooperation against my D as ruling out selfishness; D choices and public promises were not conclusive evidence of role.

P8.strategy: Cooperated to support good-player welfare; used observed defections to update identity beliefs and defected against P5 in our final encounter.

P9.strategy: Cooperated broadly to support good players’ combined payoff; treated repeated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness and updated beliefs from observed actions.

P10.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support joint gains among good players; treated observed defections as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
